name: Abdou Yaackoubi
title: Senior Product Designer
tagline: Product direction, interface craft, and an AI-assisted build practice.
intro: What holds my attention is interaction design — how a thing responds, what it does while it waits, and how it recovers. I build to find out: a prototype in code answers questions a static frame cannot.
contactLede: Senior product designer at InstaDeep. Open to conversations about product work and collaborations.
about: Today I'm a senior product designer at InstaDeep, an AI company acquired by BioNTech, working on their AI products and the design system underneath them. Before that I led product design at Steer, and at T-ledger I designed one of Tunisia's first digital wallets, built on blockchain.
Six years, four companies, and one studio of my own — fintech, automotive retail, food delivery, home services and AI.
Based in Tunis — UTC+1, the same working day as Paris and Berlin.

experience.note: AI products, and the design system every InstaDeep product surface and demo runs on.
The only person in design and product, leading the front-end and back-end engineers. The company went on to raise in France.
Sole designer across both of the company's products.

values.heading: Values I believe in
values.description: Craft is most of the job. The rest is how you behave when the work gets ambiguous, late, or contested — these are what I come back to.

items.label: Stay next to the build
items.body: Design that stops at handoff gets built as something else. At Steer I walked the developers through every screen and followed the build; at Konnect the constant back and forth with the CTO is the reason it shipped functional rather than merely drawn.

items.label: Design for the room you are not in
items.body: The InstaDeep system had to survive being used by engineers with no designer present. If a component only works while I am there to explain it, I have not finished it.

items.label: Ask for the criticism early
items.body: A review where nobody disagrees is a review that found nothing. I would rather hear it at the prototype than at the launch, and rather document a disagreement than win it quietly.

aboutBlock.label: A bit about me
aboutBlock.statement: I design products where the interface has to carry trust.
aboutBlock.body: AI, blockchain and fintech all ask someone to act on a system they cannot check for themselves. Six years of my work has been in that gap.

aboutIntro.heading:
Design is how I think.
Building is how I prove it.
paragraphs: What holds my attention is interaction design — how a thing responds, what it does while it waits, and how it recovers. The happy path is the easy half; the interesting half is everything after it.

I visualise a product as a system before I draw a screen. The structure comes first — what the states are, what can fail, what each surface is allowed to say — and the interface is what that structure looks like once it has to face someone.

Then I build it. A prototype in code answers questions a static frame cannot, and it is the fastest way to find out that a flow which reads well does not feel right. This site is the proof: my Figma, my code, and a test suite that checks its own claims.
